Quick sizing + recommendation (first pass) based on the numbers in the attached spreadsheet and common lat/throughput profiles:

Summary recommendation:
- PoC pool: provision a dedicated pool equivalent to 6 x H100-80GB (or 10 x A100-80GB vintage) with 1.5x buffer for spikes. Expect this to meet ~80–120 req/s for quantized 70B at ~350–400ms p95 with batching disabled for p95 SLO.
- Production ramp baseline: recommend a reserve of 12 x H100-80GB (or 20 x A100-80GB) for the first month of production to hit sustained ~150 req/s and provide burst headroom.
- KV cache: enable prefix caching for known prompts to reduce effective tokens by ~15–25% for reuse-heavy flows.

Operational notes:
- Soft-hold policy: we can place a 6-week soft reservation for the PoC window with an internal flag (JIRA: JIRA-OPS-7843). After 6 weeks without a signed commitment, the reservation reverts to available inventory; we can extend once subject to exec approval if there's a documented procurement delay.
- Lead time: H100 clusters require 2–3 weeks for allocation from pool to dedicated tenant if we need specialized infra; A100 pools are faster (3–5 business days) but will have higher contention.
- Cost delta: H100 baseline reduces required instance counts but has higher hourly unit cost; recommend pricing cadence reflect either fixed-per-GPU reserved rate or committed compute hours model.

Attachments: I've sketched a size/cost estimate in the attached sheet (boreal_estimate_v1.xlsx) and a PO template (boreal_po_template.pdf).

Next steps:
- I can lock a 6-week soft-hold for mid-July start (OPS ticket created: JIRA-OPS-7843).
- We should get a quick call with Boreal procurement to agree contract timing and any SLA exceptions they need.

If folks agree, I'll mark the pool and update HubSpot deal BTR-4521 with the reservation details.

- Karthik
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
